en: Hero Jose Rizal built a waterworks system in Dapitan to provide the community with safe, clean drinking water and prevent waterborne diseases.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep newborn babies warm and safe in rural areas without electricity.
Under Republic Act 9003, every Filipino citizen has the civic duty to segregate household waste to prevent dengue-causing mosquito breeding.
The Indigenous Ifugao people built stone-walled rice terraces that safely manage mountain water flow and prevent deadly soil erosion during heavy rains.
The Department of Health, an executive branch agency, monitors local food markets to ensure the meat we eat is safe from diseases.
During the Lechon Festival in Batangas, vendors must follow strict food safety rules to properly cook pork and prevent harmful bacterial infections.
The Filipino value of bayanihan helps communities safely evacuate neighbors and share emergency supplies when typhoons cause severe flooding.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council coordinates local government units to keep citizens safe during volcanic eruptions and earthquakes.
The Department of Health translates vital medical instructions into major Philippine languages like Cebuano and Ilocano to ensure patient safety.
The Department of Health scientifically tests traditional Indigenous herbal medicines like lagundi to safely treat coughs without harmful side effects.
The Anti-Bullying Act of 2013 legally requires all Philippine schools to implement safety programs that protect students from physical and cyber harm.
Protecting the habitat of the Philippine Eagle, our national bird, prevents zoonotic diseases and maintains a healthy, balanced forest ecosystem.
